Bitcoin is a form of digital currency that is based on mathematical proof and is independent of any central authority. It is created, or mined, by the community using a distributed network of computers around the world. As of today, one bitcoin is worth about $415 US dollars. Bitcoins are divided into smaller units to make transactions easier. The smallest unit is called satoshi after the founder of Bitcoin, Satoshi Nakamoto. One satoshi is equal to 0.00000001 bitcoin or one hundred-millionth of a bitcoin.

Bitcoins are cryptographically stored in digital wallets. A digital wallet is an app that allows one to send or receive Bitcoin. A wallet creates receiving addresses that can be used by others to send it bitcoin. A bitcoin address is a string of letters and numbers. For instance, the receiving address for Voat is 1BFqer7P9qqqiirbC63KqxfuZYXxk6RrBZ.

You can run a wallet on your own computer, but doing so requires the wallet to download what is called the blockchain. The blockchain is the heart of bitcoin. It is a mathematical record of every transaction ever made via bitcoin. It is a large file, currently over 60Gb. The wallet only needs to download it once and it will then update the blockchain each time the wallet is run.

An alternative to running your own wallet is to use an online wallet. These are services that will allow you to buy and store bitcoin on their servers. This allows the convenience of being able to send and receive bitcoin from any web browser or wallet mobile app. For most casual users of bitcoin, online wallets are the best and easiest solution.

Coinbase and Circle are two of the largest online wallets, but there are many others. US law requires both of these services to establish the user's identity when setting up an account. Also, payments loaded into these wallets have to be made through a bank account or bank-issued credit card or debit card. However, once you have loaded money into your bitcoin wallet with these services, any bitcoin deposits you make are completely anonymous to the receiver. This means that Voat will still not have any identifying information about you when you donate.

If privacy is paramount or if you are the type that doesn't deal with banks, it is possible to purchase bitcoin anonymously from private vendors using pre-paid debit cards. LocalBitcoins offers a service to connect private bitcoin vendors with buyers. These are independent vendors, so if you use this route, pay attention to vendor ratings and reviews.

Once you have your wallet set up and have some bitcoin in it, making payments is extremely easy. Just choose the amount you want to send and enter the receiving address. Again, the receiving address for Voat is 1BFqer7P9qqqiirbC63KqxfuZYXxk6RrBZ, which can be verified here.
